components.name: Predictor and correction from the old point
components.operation: First compute p_k=z_k-eta F(z_k), then z_{k+1}=z_k-eta F(p_k).
components.requires: Two exact operator evaluations in the full Euclidean domain and a valid block Lipschitz upper bound for tuning.
transfer_checks: A constrained domain requires a separately analyzed projected algorithm.
Noise or inexact gradients require a new error analysis.
L=max of block constants gives a joint bound 2L, not generally L.
Changing the output to the predictor or an average requires its own metric guarantee.

limitations.statement: The guarantee concerns this selected EG trajectory and output. It does not establish unrestricted Oracle Complexity, optimality, or a lower bound for other algorithms.
The printed supplementary derivation contains formula defects. The accompanying theorem supplies a separate local argument requiring independent complete_local_argument_checked review.

performance_links.scope_note: Only the specified exact EG recurrence, unconstrained model, stepsize and last-iterate squared-distance metric.

variants.cost: Exactly two joint-gradient evaluations per completed iteration, hence 2N joint queries. If partial-gradient calls are separately charged, this is two gradient_x plus two gradient_y calls per iteration. Vector arithmetic costs O(m+n) per step and O(m+n) working storage, excluding the oracle's internal cost. There are no function-value queries, projections, proximal solves or stochastic samples. These costs are operational counts from the explicit recurrence.
variants.implementation_details_ref: Main PDF p.7 Algorithm 2; main pp.3–4 assumptions; supplement p.12 Eqs.(121)–(122). Loop starts at k=0 to resolve the source box's x_0 versus k=1 indexing inconsistency.
variants.name: Algorithm 2 with Theorem 7 tuning
variants.output: Return the last full iterate z_N=(x_N,y_N), not a predictor, average or randomly selected iterate. Every point lies in the unconstrained product space.
public_inputs: Dimensions m,n; initial point z_0=(x_0,y_0) in R^m x R^n; exact access to both partial gradients.
Known L>0 bounding all four block Lipschitz constants; choose eta=1/(8L).
A chosen finite iteration budget N. The update itself does not require mu or the unknown saddle.
variants.query_and_update: Let F(x,y)=(gradient_x f(x,y),-gradient_y f(x,y)). Query F(z_k) and form p_k=z_k-eta F(z_k): p_x=x_k-eta gradient_x f(x_k,y_k), p_y=y_k+eta gradient_y f(x_k,y_k). Query F(p_k), then set z_{k+1}=z_k-eta F(p_k): x_{k+1}=x_k-eta gradient_x f(p_x,p_y), y_{k+1}=y_k+eta gradient_y f(p_x,p_y). Both corrections start from z_k.
variants.requirements: f:R^m x R^n -> R is continuously differentiable and has a saddle. Uniformly over the other block, f(.,y) is mu_x-strongly convex and f(x,.) is mu_y-strongly concave with mu_x,mu_y>0. gradient_x is L_x-Lipschitz in x and L_xy-Lipschitz in y; gradient_y is L_y-Lipschitz in y and L_yx-Lipschitz in x. Each constant is at most L. Queries return exact joint gradients at arbitrary points in the full product space.
variants.state_and_initialization: Store an arbitrary z_0=(x_0,y_0). For k=0,...,N-1 keep the old point z_k while constructing the predictor p_k. No previous gradient, warm start or initialization query is required.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: Use eta=1/(8L) for the selected contraction. Run a supplied integer budget N>=0; the source box is an indefinite loop and does not provide an observable error certificate. If a certified initial squared-distance bound R>=r_0 and mu=min(mu_x,mu_y)>0 are additionally supplied, the theorem's local corollary gives the sufficient budget ceil(8(L/mu) log(R/epsilon)) for 0<epsilon<R. This is a corollary, not a source-specified stopping test.

use_restrictions: Selected deterministic unconstrained variant only; performance depends on the accompanying theorem and its review.
The source's loop indexing and Assumption 3 gradient-subscript issues are explicitly resolved as documented; no claim that the printed box is internally consistent.
No independent review or publication is claimed.

summary: Unconstrained deterministic EG with two exact joint-gradient queries per iteration, arbitrary initialization and stepsize 1/(8L) for the selected strongly convex–strongly concave guarantee.
title: Extragradient for a strongly convex–strongly concave saddle
use_when: Compute a saddle by predictor-corrector gradient steps when all four block Lipschitz constants have a known upper bound.
